messages.author: f5bec70b36df06aa
messages.subject: Merging two boxplot graphs
parts:
Hi @ all

I have the following two separate graphs with boxplots showing the
distribution of nutrients per season and catchment: graph 1 =
catchment one, graph 2 = catchment 2.
Is there a chance that I can merge both graphs into one showing the
following: boxplots in color 1 show nutrient distribution for
catchment one during dry season; boxplots in color 2 show nutrient
distribution for catchment one during wet season; boxplots in color 3
show nutrient distribution for catchment two during dry season; and
boxplots in color 4 show nutrient distribution for catchment two
during wet season? I tried to use group=catchment or group=season in
ggplot but it didn't work.

Thanks for your ideas in advance.

Cheers
Martin


#Graph 1 showing catchment 1
dodge <- position_dodge(width = .8)

read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/nutrients_all.csv") ->
nutrients_sw

names(nutrients_sw)=c("ID","round","Season","catchment","Nitrite
N","Nitrate N","Ammonium N","Organic N","Orthophosphate","Total P")

melt_nutrients_sw <- melt(nutrients_sw, id=c("ID", "round", "Season",
"catchment"),na.rm=TRUE)
subset_melt <- subset(melt_nutrients_sw, catchment=="1" & ID<=60)

subset_melt$catchment<-factor(subset_melt$catchment)
p <- ggplot(subset_melt, aes(x = variable, y = value, color =
Season))
p + geom_boxplot(position=dodge, width=0.5) +
opts(legend.background=theme_rect(colour=NA)) + theme_bw() +
opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour="white")) + xlab("") +
ylab("mg/L") + opts(plot.background = theme_rect(colour = "black"))

#Graph 2 showing catchment 2
dodge <- position_dodge(width = .8)

read.csv("http://dl.dropbox.com/u/4236038/nutrients_all.csv") ->
nutrients_sw

names(nutrients_sw)=c("ID","round","Season","catchment","Nitrite
N","Nitrate N","Ammonium N","Organic N","Orthophosphate","Total P")

melt_nutrients_sw <- melt(nutrients_sw, id=c("ID", "round", "Season",
"catchment"),na.rm=TRUE)
subset_melt <- subset(melt_nutrients_sw, catchment=="2" & ID<=60)

subset_melt$catchment<-factor(subset_melt$catchment)
p <- ggplot(subset_melt, aes(x = variable, y = value, color =
Season))
p + geom_boxplot(position=dodge, width=0.5) +
opts(legend.background=theme_rect(colour=NA)) + theme_bw() +
opts(legend.key=theme_rect(fill=NULL,colour="white")) + xlab("") +
ylab("mg/L") + opts(plot.background = theme_rect(colour = "black"))

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Merging two boxplot graphs
parts:
A poorman' version is to create a new variable by merging Season and catchment.

subset_melt <- subset(melt_nutrients_sw, catchment%in%c("1","2") & ID<=60)
subset_melt$col<-paste(subset_melt$Season, subset_melt$catchment) #
merge by paste
p <- ggplot(subset_melt, aes(x = variable, y = value, color=col))
p + geom_boxplot(position=dodge, width=0.5)

This will make sense because you think the new factor with 4 levels.
If you think data with 2 x 2 factors, then it may be better to use
'fill' or something else like this.

p <- ggplot(subset_melt, aes(x = variable, y = value, color=Season,
fill=factor(catchment)))
p + geom_boxplot(position=dodge, width=0.5)

It makes clear that your data has 2 x 2 factors.

There may be more elegant way, but I don't know.

HTH
